---
title: "Keys on Shared Ground"
---

::: {.ao-story}
Your home directory lies on ground that others can reach. Keys, tokens and agent settings lie there too, in plain files, and shared ground has many passers-by. Before the agent works here, find out who can read what it leaves behind.
:::

::: {.quest-dialog}
- **Goal:** you will keep keys and agent settings private on shared storage, keep data within its agreement, and know what to ask your cluster staff.
- **Before you start:** [Login Node Manners](login-node-manners.html) and [The Locked Cabinet](../crypt/secrets-and-sensitive-ground.html). *Egress* means data leaving the machine.
- **Time:** about 15 minutes.
:::

You need this before you run an agent under your cluster account: keys and agent settings live in ordinary files, and on a shared cluster other people may be able to read them. It covers Claude Code only, and keeping them private and keeping data within its agreement. Ask your cluster staff before sending any cluster data to an external model API, and follow your institution's data agreement. This quest is read-only, so read it on your laptop.

## What lives where

Claude Code keeps sessions, settings and plugins in the folder `~/.claude`. It also writes the file `~/.claude.json`, which holds account details, MCP configuration (the list of external tool servers you connected) and trust decisions. The environment variable `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` moves the `~/.claude` folder elsewhere.

If your home directory is shared across nodes, session history sits on shared storage and can contain pasted data or paths. Check who can read the folder:

```bash
ls -ld ~/.claude
```

Safe looks like `drwx------`: only you can read, write or enter it. Any `r` or `x` in the last six characters means a group or other users can get in. Fix it with `chmod 700 ~/.claude`. To see what the output looks like, make a folder in a scratch location, run `chmod 700` on it, and run `ls -ld` on it. Also ask whether home is backed up or group-readable.

Two settings files are yours to control: user `~/.claude/settings.json` (all your projects) and project `.claude/settings.json` (commit it for the team). Managed settings (settings an organisation sets for everyone) override both, so your site may already have decided some of this.

## Keys

- `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, when set, overrides a subscription login. In `-p` mode (one prompt, no interactive session) it is always used, and interactive mode asks you once to approve it. If a key is exported in a shared profile, the key in use may not be the one you expect.
- Never put a key in a script or in a committed `.claude/settings.json`. On a shared account, use a per-user key kept in a file readable only by you (mode 600, set with `chmod 600 <file>`; `ls -l` then shows `-rw-------`), and keep a lab-wide key out of shared directories.
- The sandbox's default reads cover most of the machine, including credential files such as `~/.ssh` and `~/.aws/credentials`. The sandbox is the restricted environment Claude Code runs shell commands in. To block key files, add a `Read(...)` deny rule (a permission rule that stops the agent's file-read tool, such as `Read(~/.ssh/**)`) and the `sandbox.filesystem.denyRead` setting (a list of paths the sandbox hides from shell commands). The sandbox covers shell commands only, so you need both.

`apiKeyHelper` is a Claude Code setting that runs a shell script you provide and uses the key it returns, so the key need not sit in a file. This page covers Claude Code only. For OpenCode, read your version's docs on where it stores keys before you use it on a shared account.

## Data and egress

- Before any cluster data, paths, logs or code go to an external model API, check your institution's policy. Human genomic, clinical or controlled-access data often has agreements that forbid third-party processing.
- Reading files inside the working directory is approved without asking, so the agent can read a project folder that holds controlled data unless a `Read(...)` deny rule or `sandbox.filesystem.denyRead` covers it. Keep controlled data outside the agent's working directory and give the agent synthetic or de-identified test data.
- Some sites restrict internet access from compute nodes, so an agent there may not reach a model API. Ask staff what outbound access your jobs have. A common pattern is the agent on your laptop writing scripts, with jobs running offline.
- A plain `ssh` from inside the Claude Code sandbox cannot reach another host.
- The sandbox's `network.allowedDomains` starts empty, so unlisted hosts prompt (in the default modes).

::: {.panel-tabset group="companion"}

## Claude Code

If your project has an instruction file (`AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`) stricter than these notes, the stricter one wins, and your cluster's policy outranks both. Ask staff these before use: is an external model API allowed for my data, which tools are allowed on login nodes, what outbound access exists, and where are my home and scratch backed up and who can read them? For restricted networks, `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC=1` turns off auto-updates, telemetry, error reporting and feedback traffic.

## OpenCode + Ollama

The same questions apply. Ask staff whether a local model through Ollama changes what your data agreement requires, and whether running one on a login node is allowed, since models are heavy.

:::

## Lore

*Further reading. Optional.*

- [Configure the sandboxed Bash tool](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it states the sandbox reads most of the machine, including ~/.ssh, unless you deny it, and it fails open by default.
- [Configure permissions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it explains how settings files apply and combine by scope, so you can see which level should hold deny rules for your keys; it warns Bash rules are not a security boundary.
- [Security](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it covers credential storage and advice for sensitive code, relevant to where keys sit on shared storage.
:::
